info.summary: Versioned HTTP contract for every core feature of the Togavsu practice-management system.
info.description: Proposal for /api/v1, the unauthenticated agent card at /llms.txt, and the MCP transport at /mcp. Handlers are not part of this document. Money is integer cents. Identifiers are UUIDv7. Timestamps are UTC. Lists use an opaque cursor. Errors are application/problem+json. See docs/api/conventions.md.

post.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint. initialize and tools/list describe the tools and need no credential. tools/call runs one OpenAPI operation: params.name is the operationId, and params.arguments carries path parameters, query parameters, idempotency_key, and body. Authorization is decided from that operation before any effect. A public operation, including first-run setup, login, and TOTP enrollment, is reachable with no session and no bearer. Every other tool requires the same session cookie or bearer as its HTTP operation. An invalid credential is unauthenticated. Cookie and bearer together are ambiguous_auth. Arguments must not carry Authorization, Host, or roles. A tool error uses the problem body and sets the JSON-RPC error data to that problem.

post.description: Creates the firm and the first admin, then returns an enrollment challenge with otpauth_uri and the TOTP secret. No session cookie is set. The next call is confirmTotpEnrollment. A later setup call returns already_set_up.

Password check. No session cookie is set until TOTP is confirmed. A user who already enrolled gets status totp_required. A user who has not enrolled gets status enrollment_required and enrollment_token, then calls startTotpEnrollment. Repeated failures lock the account.
Exchanges a totp_token and a code for a session. This is only for a user who already finished enrollment. The first enrollment uses confirmTotpEnrollment.

post.summary: Start TOTP enrollment before a session
post.description: Public. Takes the enrollment_token from a login whose status is enrollment_required. Returns otpauth_uri and the secret once. Does not set a session.

post.summary: Confirm TOTP enrollment and open a session
post.description: Public. Confirms the first code for the enrollment_token from setup or startTotpEnrollment. Sets the session cookie and returns the initial recovery codes once. An authenticated reset uses resetTotp and confirmTotpReset, not this step.

Starts a replacement enrollment for the signed-in user. The current secret stays active until confirmTotpReset accepts the first code. The response includes a single-use enrollment_token that expires. Another user's reset is not_found.

Activates the pending secret for the signed-in user and then invalidates the old one. The enrollment_token is the one resetTotp returned, and it is spent by a correct code. A wrong code, an expired token, or a replay does not change the active secret. A token issued for another user is forbidden.
Replaces the user's recovery codes. The new codes are returned once.

post.description: An approved module token with markers:write registers one marker in its own namespace. The owner is the signed module id on the token. The path module_id must be that same id. A caller-supplied owner is ignored. The token cannot create a firm marker or a marker for another module. settings:write and an admin role are not accepted here. A human session is forbidden. The label is plain text. The color is a six-digit hex value. An optional display target is a module-local page; a URL or another scheme is rejected. A second active marker with the same label in this namespace is a conflict. Revoke hides the definition and leaves matter pins that already use it.

patch.description: Updates the calling module's own marker. A firm marker and another module's marker are forbidden. The signed module id is the owner. A duplicate active label in this namespace is a conflict. A revoked marker is not edited back to active; register a new one. Label, color, and display target use the same checks as createModuleMarker.

post.description: Sets the calling module's marker inactive. The row stays, and matter pins that already use it stay. A firm marker and another module's marker are forbidden. Revoking an inactive marker returns the original result and emits nothing.

A staff session asks the core to authorize one installed processor for this matter, contact, amount, and destination. The core delivers processor_authorization on moduleEvent payment.processor_authorized to that module only. This call does not create a payment and does not post trust. The initiation response does not contain the grant. An unregistered module, a different recipient, or a module id that is not the processor receives no grant. A walled matter the caller cannot see is not_found and issues nothing. Operating needs payments:write on the caller and on the module. Trust also needs trust:write on both, checked before delivery. The grant is not an admin or firm-wide token. The later callback does not need an iframe or a signed-in viewer.

Pending may become completed or failed. The same status is idempotent and does not write. Completed, failed, and reversed are terminal here. A late callback that would leave a terminal status is conflict and changes neither the payment nor the ledger. A settled correction is reversePayment, not status failed. reversed cannot become completed. The amount does not change. A registered processor calls this with the core-issued grant and no viewer session. The payment id, matter, and amount must be the ones bound on that grant. The first completion of a trust destination needs trust:write before any ledger row is written. A later completion does not post a second row. An ambient payments:write token with no viewer and no grant is forbidden. payment.completed is emitted when pending becomes completed. A change to failed emits payment.updated and not payment.completed. A same-status replay emits nothing.

Posts a reversal. The original payment amount is not edited and the original trust row is not edited. An operating payment, one with no trust entry, needs payments:write. A trust-linked payment also needs trust:withdraw. That scope check runs before any payment status change and before any ledger write. Insufficient scopes, the wrong role, or a walled matter write nothing. When the scopes and the wall allow it, the trust handler appends exactly one reversal. The time module does not post another. A reversal that leaves a negative balance still posts and raises trust.flag_raised. A non-negative reversal does not raise the flag. Rollback, denial, and replay emit nothing.

A trust:write token is scope_denied for a withdrawal, transfer, refund, or adjustment in the batch, and nothing is posted. There is no bulk edit and no bulk delete.

A repeated id rejects the batch and writes nothing. Publication is one transaction: every new file and first version is created, or none are. After that transaction commits, each newly published version emits file.version_created. An upload that already has a file is an atomic replay: the original file is returned and no publication event or grant is added. A failed item returns batch_rejected, leaves every upload staged, and emits no file.created, no file.version_created, and no scan grant.

post.summary: Deliver a signed event to a subscribed module.
post.description: Before any WebhookEvent body is serialized, the core checks that the module is installed, subscribed to the event type, approved for that event's read scope, and allowed through the matter wall. An attorney-only conflict record is not serialized. A module that fails any check receives no POST and no record id or summary. The core POSTs the event only after those checks, and only to an installed module whose manifest event_subscriptions include the event type. X-Togavsu-Signature is sha256= plus the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body bytes, keyed with the module webhook secret. A plain SHA-256 of the body is not accepted. X-Togavsu-Timestamp is unix seconds. Retries follow webhooks.retry_attempts across webhooks.retry_window_hours. The starting values are 8 attempts and 24 hours. For file.version_created the core also sends X-Togavsu-Task-Authorization and task_authorization in the body. That grant is issued by the core for this delivery's module id, event, file, and version. It names the operations and metadata fields the module may call with no iframe and no viewer context. The module presents the same grant on those later calls. An expired grant, a revoked grant, or a grant whose signature does not check is forbidden. A revoked module bearer is unauthenticated. A different module id is forbidden. Another matter, file, or version is not_found. An operation outside the grant is forbidden. A field outside the grant is field_locked. An attorney-only field stays not_found. The approved scopes on each operation are still required. The grant is not an admin or firm-wide bypass. file.background_authorized delivers background_file_authorization to the installed module that holds files:write. That grant is one matter the service principal can access, the publication sequence, and an expiry. payment.processor_authorized delivers processor_authorization the same way, to the registered processor only. That grant binds the initialization, payment, matter, contact, amount, and destination. createPayment and updatePaymentStatus may use it with no iframe and no signed-in viewer. An unregistered processor receives no grant. A missing, expired, or revoked grant is forbidden and writes no payment.

Next invoice sequence value.
Payment terms in days.

Day of the month for the reconciliation reminder.

Default event reminder offsets, in days before the start.
iCal feeds are served when true. Revoking a link is separate.
Default end date is this many months after the start.
Default purpose line on an available-dates pleading or letter.
Default title on an available-dates pleading.
Largest accepted upload.

Folder names copied onto a new matter from its practice area when that area has no override.

Edit lock lapses after this long without a renewal.
Editor runs allowed at once.
Time limit for one editor run.
Memory limit for one editor run.
Write a PDF preview rendition when a version is saved.

File naming pattern. A status token is refused. The naming endpoint reads and writes this same setting.
Confidence below this sends the item to review.
Quiet time before photos of one matter are grouped.

Review-queue email recipients. Empty means the admins.
Send the Doc Tender daily summary.
Local time of the daily summary. Firm time zone.
Bundle new-exception email to at most one message per this interval.

An unexplained transcript gap longer than this fails the coverage check.
Window used when a second transcription is compared.
Seconds between described video frames.
Named layouts a user may save. The next one is refused.

Hit cap for each scope when the scope is All.

SMTP host for system mail.

SMTP username.
Use STARTTLS for system mail.
When true and an email module is installed, system mail is handed to that module.
Problem-report recipients. Empty means the admins.

Heading font.
Body font.

Fast model on the primary provider.

Strong model on the secondary provider.

Doc Tender transcription check model.

Labeling check model. A local endpoint is refused.

Categorizing check model. A local endpoint is refused.
Update window start, firm local time.
Update window end, firm local time.
When true, scheduled updates do not run. Update now still requires an admin action.
Nightly backup time, firm local time.
Days a backup stays on the local backup volume.
Day of the month for the test restore.
Application and access log retention. The audit log is kept forever and is not this setting.
Webhook delivery attempts.
Window that holds the webhook attempts.
Include the firm name on /llms.txt.
One optional paragraph of firm text on /llms.txt. It must not contain client or matter records.
Default rows per API page unless the list has its own page-size setting. The effective size is limited by api.max_page_size. Default 50. A change applies on the next read and is audited.
Maximum rows per API page for lists using general pagination. Default 200. A change applies on the next read and is audited.
How long a stored Idempotency-Key result is replayed. The PRD requires the header and does not name the retention; 24 hours is the starting value.
Maximum items in one bulk request. The PRD requires one transaction and does not name a cap; 500 is the starting value.
Maximum rows in one CSV response. A larger filter returns validation_failed. Starting value is a contract choice.
Marketplace base URL. Empty disables browse and leaves local-file install working. The PRD default is the Togavsu marketplace; the host is set when that service is deployed.
How often the core polls the marketplace for flags and pulls.
Module id that handles the time domain. Empty means the core.
Module id that handles the trust domain. Empty means the core. A replacing module still raises the below-zero flag.
Module id that handles the calendar domain. Empty means the core.
